term_types.name: Deanonymisation / tracing approach
term_types.question: What technique is used to trace or link pseudonymous transactions back to identities?
term_types.description: Method by which a pseudonymous ledger's transfers are clustered, labelled or attributed to real-world actors by investigators or detectors.

term_types.name: Backing mechanism
term_types.question: How is the backing asset held or secured against the token?
term_types.description: Distinguishes whether backing assets are held in custody, pledged or locked, or governed by an oracle or algorithm.
values: custodial reserve held by third party
pledged or encumbered on a ledger

term_types.name: Settlement finality timing
term_types.question: When does the payment become final relative to its initiation?
term_types.description: Distinguishes whether settlement is immediate, deferred to a batch or net window, or triggered by a condition or event.

term_types.name: Settlement counterparty
term_types.question: Which entity actually moves the fiat funds to the merchant or seller?
term_types.description: Identifies the institution or platform that performs the fiat-side payout, distinct from the crypto-side transfer.

term_types.name: Physical transfer mechanism across air gap
term_types.question: By what physical channel, if any, is data moved across the isolation boundary between the key-holding device and the network?
term_types.description: Distinguishes how signed or key material physically crosses an air gap, which the existing binary-style values do not separate.
merged_from: physical transfer mechanism across air gap

term_types.name: Validator selection mechanism
term_types.question: How are the validators or consensus nodes chosen for a given round?
term_types.description: Describes how the set of active validators is selected, independent of who is eligible to join.

term_types.name: Sharding partition basis
term_types.question: On what basis is the ledger or validator set partitioned into shards?
term_types.description: Describes what criterion divides the network or state into parallel shards.

term_types.name: Wallet interface or delivery form
term_types.question: In what form or interface is the wallet's key material delivered to or accessed by the user?
term_types.description: Classifies the physical or software form in which the wallet and its keys are presented to the user.

term_types.name: Share recovery mechanism
term_types.question: How can the divided key shares be recombined or recovered if some shares are lost or unavailable?
term_types.description: Distinguishes how split key material is reconstituted, such as threshold reconstruction, escrow recovery, or dynamic re-sharing.

term_types.name: Centralisation locus
term_types.question: Which component or layer of the system is centralised (consensus/mining, block building, governance, token issuance, data storage, or validation)?
term_types.description: Splits centralisation by the specific layer where control concentrates, rather than an overall level.

term_types.name: Cross-chain interoperability mechanism
term_types.question: How does the mechanism move state or value between blockchains?
term_types.description: Technique used to transfer or verify assets, data, or transactions across distinct blockchain networks.

values.definition: Key shares are held by nodes of a blockchain or decentralized network, such that a threshold of nodes must cooperate to reconstruct the key.

values.value: backed by physical commodities or precious metals
values.definition: The token's value is backed by physical commodities, precious metals, gems or other tangible goods held in custody.
The crypto settlement is triggered by a payment card whose authorization flows through a card network.
Fiat settlement is replaced by settlement tokens or in-network tokens on a distributed ledger rather than a bridged rail.

values.value: NFT minting for media and content licensing
values.definition: Units minted as NFTs representing a media asset, royalty split, or content authorisation, typically via a marketplace or digital vault.
Private keys are generated and stored on a device never connected to a network, with signing performed offline via QR codes, cards, or isolated chambers.
Non-fungible token issued under a smart-contract standard, such as ERC-721 or ERC-1155, representing unique assets.
